rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT method (GGA geometry optimization, total energies, frontier orbital energies) applied to well-defined molecular models. The only mild nuance is the effective work function definition, but the overall method is textbook and widely implemented in codes like SIESTA.
rationale.execution: A straightforward pipeline: build structures, run a few DFT optimizations (8 models can be scripted sequentially or in parallel), compute chemical potentials, and extract tabular results. No complex multi-tool orchestration or fragile data assembly.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT (GGA/BLYP with a DZP-quality basis) to small CNT models of 150–183 atoms. The reproduction task is to run geometry optimizations and extract HOMO/LUMO/formation energies — a routine computational chemistry workflow. No novel algorithms or complex pipeline orchestration.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small CNT models (≤183 atoms) with a GGA functional and a double-zeta basis set; total energy calculations require only modest CPU memory and no large datasets.
